summary: Gustaf John Ramstedt worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his M.A. at the University of Helsinki (~1893–1898) under Otto Donner, J. N. Reuter, and Eemil Nestor Setälä, later serving there as professor (1917–1941) and at the University of Tokyo (~1919–1929).

Gustav Bickell specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg (1857) and earned his Ph.D. at Marburg (1857–1862). He held posts at Marburg, Giessen, Münster, Innsbruck (Professor ord., 1874), and Vienna (Professor of Semitic Languages, 1891).

Gustav Ecke worked in Sinology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Bonn, Berlin, Erlangen-Nuremberg (Ph.D. 1914–1922), and under Joseph Hackin, he taught at Xiamen, Tsinghua, and Fu Jen Catholic University before holding posts at the Honolulu Museum of Art and University of Hawaiʻi.

Gustav Friedrich Oehler worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Tübingen, under Ludwig Heinrich Kapff, and in Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held teaching posts at Basel Mission Seminary, Tübingen, Evangelical Seminary of Schöntal, and the University of Breslau.

Gustav Haloun specialized in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under August Conrady at Leipzig and completed habilitations at Prague. He directed at Göttingen (1931–1938) and held the Chair of Chinese Language and History at Cambridge (1938–1951).

Gustav Herbig was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Munich, completing his Ph.D. and habilitation at Munich. He worked as a librarian at the Bavarian State Library (1899–1913) and served as ordinary professor at Rostock, Breslau, and Munich.

Gustav Mensching worked in religious, Buddhist, and Indological studies. He studied at Göttingen, Berlin, Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel, and Marburg under Rudolf Otto and Friedrich Heiler. He held posts at Marburg, the University of Latvia (1927–1935), Kiel (1935–1936), and Bonn (1936–1969).

Gustav Meyer was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. After teaching posts at Ernestinum Gotha, Kleinseitner Gymnasium, and Charles University, he served as associate professor at the University of Graz (1877–1897).

Gustav Roth specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Breslau, Leipzig, Halle-Wittenberg, Munich, and Patna under teachers including Friedrich Weller and Helmut Hoffmann, he served at the University of Göttingen (1965–1981) and directed the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Gustav Salomon Oppert worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied in Bonn, Berlin, Leipzig, and Halle-Wittenberg (Ph.D.). He held posts at the Bodleian and Royal Libraries, Presidency University (1872–1894), the University of Berlin, and the Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums.

Gustave Liétard was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Collège de Toul and earned his Dr.med. at the University of Strasbourg (~1852–1858), studying under Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann and Philippe Édouard Foucaux.
Gustavo Benavides is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who held an affiliation at Villanova University, attested in 1995 and 2004.

Gustavo Moura works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned a bachelor's degree at the University of Chester (2013–2016), a master's at Federal University of Paraíba (2015–2017), and a Ph.D. in Religious Studies at Wilfrid Laurier University (2018–2022).

Gustaw Blatt was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Jagiellonian University under Lucjan Malinowski and at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann, Ernst Windisch, and August Leskien. He taught at Jewish Gymnasium, Brody, and became a professor at the University of Lviv.

Guus Kroonen is a linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (~2004–2009). He held positions at the University of Copenhagen (~2013) and at the Leiden University Centre for Linguistics (2016).

Guy Bugault worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Having studied under Olivier Lacombe, he held posts at Paris Nanterre University (~1964–1968) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1968–1985), where he was Professor of Indian and Comparative Philosophy.

Guy G. Stroumsa works in religious studies. He studied at Paris, Hebrew University, Harvard (M.A., Ph.D.), and EPHE. He held faculty posts at Hebrew University (from 1978) and served as professor at the University of Oxford (2009–2013).

Guy Newland specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and traditional teachers. He held a post as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).
Guybon Henry Damant worked in linguistics and Indology. He completed an M.A. at Christ's College, Cambridge (1864–1868), where he studied under John Peile and Edward Byles Cowell.
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
